absent: Full struct layouts for cred and user_struct and user_namespace and task credential linkage and their locking beyond what fragments show.
Numeric values of arch crash bounds and alignment and default low size and page size and CMA range capacity.
Memblock allocation and free semantics and failure modes beyond null return.
Contiguous allocator base and size accessor contracts and declaration failure modes.
Security and keyring and group and uid and counting hook contracts beyond call presence.
Template sysctl table contents and registration lifetime.
Callers and boot ordering of crash parsing and reservation and credential init entries.
Concurrency protection for crash descriptors and contiguous array and count.
Signal and cgroup and IPC behaviors implied by dossier title but absent from these fragments.

findings.text: Crash reservation parsing and generic allocation and contiguous tracking storage are visible outside their file for early boot use, with two mutually exclusive builds supplying the same contiguous entry so exactly one is present per configuration.

Credential and user identity and namespace helpers cited here are visible outside their defining files for task lifecycle and privilege management, covering release and exit and allocation and duplication and comparison and namespace creation and counting refresh.

Range list parsing first rounds the supplied total upward to a fixed large granularity to tolerate firmware reserved holes. It then walks comma separated entries each giving a start bound with optional end bound and a reservation size, requiring dash and colon separators and strictly increasing bounds and a size below the rounded total. The first entry whose interval contains the rounded total supplies the result size, with an optional at sign suffix after the chosen entry supplying an explicit base. Any missing numeric field or wrong separator or inverted interval fails.

Classic form accepts a single size with optional at sign base. It requires a leading numeric field and allows only blank or end after the size or after the base, failing on any other trailing character. No interval matching occurs in this form.
Suffix selector codes are small integers with high as zero and low as one and contiguous as two and null terminator as three. They index the suffix table.

Suffix spellings are comma followed by high for the high selector and comma followed by low for the low selector and comma followed by cma for the contiguous selector, with a null entry terminating the table.

Command lookup retains the final crashkernel occurrence, skipping entries that end with any known suffix when no suffix is requested and keeping only entries ending with the requested suffix otherwise. Suffixed parsing demands a leading size immediately followed by the exact expected spelling and then blank or end. Dispatch clears both outputs and requires valid output locations, then selects suffixed parsing when a suffix is requested, else extended interval parsing when a colon appears before any blank, else classic parsing, propagating absence when no keyword is found.

Top level parsing first attempts the plain form. On generic reservation builds with a high indicator supplied and no plain setting found, it attempts high then low suffixed forms with a default low size when the low form is absent, marking high placement on success. An optional contiguous size is parsed independently with its base ignored. Empty results and sizes reaching total memory are rejected.
A boot parameter placeholder accepts its argument and succeeds without action, preserving compatibility for a recognized but inert option.

Low reservation on wide builds allocates the requested length with required alignment constrained to a low arch window starting at zero. Failure is reported without side effects. Success records an inclusive interval in a dedicated low descriptor and may publish it to the global memory resource tree early on some builds.

Generic reservation chooses an initial window from explicit base versus high flag versus default low. It attempts allocation with required alignment inside that window. Explicit base failure ends without fallback. Default low failure retries once across the high window while ensuring a default low extra. High failure retries once inside low when distinct. Success with a high placed main region triggers low extra allocation and rolls back the main region if that extra fails. Otherwise it records the main descriptor and excludes involved pages from leak scanning and may publish early.

Contiguous extras use a fixed capacity array of inclusive start and end intervals plus a count of valid entries. Capacity is a compile time constant. Count starts at zero and grows only on successful chunk reservation.

Supported contiguous reservation rounds the request up to page granularity and accumulates chunks until the request is covered or capacity or page floor is reached. Each attempt asks for the current chunk size, and failure halves that size with rounding and retries. Successful chunks append their derived interval and advance the count and accounted total. Partial coverage warns while full coverage logs success. Zero request does nothing.
Unsupported build variant performs no allocation and warns only when a nonzero contiguous request is present.

Late publication checks an arch hook and returns early when the arch handles insertion. Otherwise it publishes each of the main and low descriptors to the global memory resource tree only when the descriptor holds a nonempty interval.
Credential diagnostic prefix is the word CRED followed by colon and space, prepended to local log formats.
Credential objects come from a dedicated slab cache pointer that is the sole allocation source for later credentials. The pointer is created once at boot.
Boot initialization creates the credential slab with hardware alignment and accounting and panic on failure.

Final release demands a zero usage count and panics or traps otherwise. It also forbids releasing either current task pointer. Non deferred credentials are freed inline while others are deferred through read copy update. All attached ownership including security and keyring family and group and user and counting and namespace is released before the object returns to its slab.

User structure release uses atomic decrement with irq saved hash locking to decide final free. Final free removes the hash node while holding the hash lock and releases that lock on exit, then tears down per user state and returns the object to its cache. Null input is ignored.

Hash removal detaches the user hash node. Per user epoll teardown destroys the watch counter only on builds with epoll support and does nothing otherwise. Final user free combines hash removal with epoll teardown and cache return.

Task exit clears both credential pointers under the task and drops the associated references, using a double drop when both pointers alias the same object and single drops otherwise. An optional cached requested key is also released and cleared when that cache is configured.

Blank allocation returns a zeroed credential with usage set to one after successful security initialization. Allocation or security failure yields null with no leak, cleaning the partial object on security failure.

Execution preparation starts from a duplicated credential and then drops thread and process keyrings without replacement. Saved and filesystem identity fields are synchronized from the effective identity fields.

Cloning either shares the parent credential or installs a fresh duplicate. Sharing applies only to thread creation when the parent lacks a thread keyring, taking two extra references and accounting the new task. Otherwise a fresh duplicate is prepared, optionally creating a new user namespace with refreshed counting, adjusting keyrings so thread siblings may obtain a fresh thread ring while non thread children lose the process ring, then installing the duplicate with accounting and namespace references. Allocation or namespace failures abort with an error and no install.

Counting refresh keeps the existing counter when namespace and user identity are unchanged, avoiding table lookup, otherwise allocating a new counter and swapping it with release of the old, failing when allocation fails. Namespace acquisition takes an active reference on the user namespace reachable from the task real credential.

User namespace creation rejects excessive nesting depth and chrooted callers and callers lacking parent mappings for owner and group, plus security denial and allocation failure. Failures report resource exhaustion or permission or memory errors and unwind the namespace usage count.

On success the child records parent linkage with incremented level and ownership from effective identities and a deferred free worker and saturated counter maxima with selected live rlimit values inherited. The parent group allowance flag is copied. Keyring linkage is initialized when configured and sysctls are registered. The new credential is reset to default secure bits with full namespaced capabilities and empty ambient set and cleared request authentication, then attached and published to the namespace tree. Counting wrappers increment and decrement the namespace counter, and process number limit inheritance uses infinity for root in the initial namespace and the current limit otherwise.
Parent flag inheritance holds a dedicated state mutex only across the flag copy, not across allocation or registration.

Sysctl setup validates table size at compile time and establishes a private set, duplicates the template table, wires each entry data pointer to the corresponding namespace maximum, and registers under the user name. Allocation or registration failure cleans the set and reports false, while builds without sysctl always succeed.

Filesystem credential comparison defines a total order that first compares filesystem user then filesystem group then group set presence and size then each group in order, returning negative or zero or positive accordingly and short circuiting on identity or shared group storage.

Kernel credential factory duplicates a chosen daemon credential with fresh usage and additional references for user and namespace and group and counts, clearing keyring family and security state for later hooks, then runs security preparation. Null daemon or allocation or counting or security failure yields null with proper release of partial references.
